Cc: procurement@northridgebank.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: control provenance & evidence transfer for SOC2/ISO/SIG

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the earlier call. As part of our procurement / audit intake for FY27, NorthRidge needs a short plan that explains how Redwood will provide control provenance and evidence artifacts for SOC 2 (Type II), ISO 27001 scoping, and the SIG questionnaire. Specifically we need:

- A manifest of the artifacts you can provide (executed procedures, config snapshots, retention logs).
- A chain-of-custody / provenance statement (who collected, who stored, and timestamps).
- Transfer method for sensitive evidence (SFTP, secure drive link, or customer-controlled upload).
- A sampling strategy for telemetry/logs (90-day window requested; we may ask for a 7-day sample initially).
- Point of contact and expected SLAs for responding to follow-on evidence requests (48–72h preferred).

Attached is the RFP addendum that lists a few extra asks (retention exceptions and escrow language). Can your security team respond with a short playbook by EOD next Wednesday?

Appreciate it — we want to keep the procurement timeline tight.

Best,
Ellen Park
Procurement Lead, NorthRidge Bank
ellen.park@northridgebank.com
(415) 555-0128

3) Secure transfer options (short-lived Drive share, SFTP with one-time creds, or customer-upload portal).
4) Telemetry sampling plan (we'll propose a 7-day sample first, then the 90-day slice if needed).
5) Response SLA and escalation contacts.

Looping in Karthik and Marissa to draft the technical and assurance pieces. Kimberly from Legal will review any retention/escrow exceptions — copying her for visibility.

Folks — draft technical clarifications below that we'll include in the playbook. I'll take ownership of the telemetry and log sampling section. Key points to confirm with NorthRidge: 

- Artifact types we can provide: config snapshots (VM/container images), IAM role change logs, KMS key rotation records (not private key material), access-control proof (privileged access review logs), and signed policy PDFs.
- For telemetry we export bearer-neutral logs (no PII) and can provide time-windowed slices with SHA256 checksums for provenance.
- We can timestamp evidence with our internal NTP-synced collectors and include hash chains in the manifest.
- Transfer modes: prefer short-lived, tenant-scoped Google Drive share (we can automate creation) or SFTP to your firewall-routed endpoint.

I'll attach the preliminary evidence_manifest.csv with column headers: artifact_id, control_mapping, custodian, collected_at_utc, file_hash, storage_location. Marissa: can you confirm who from Assurance will sign the chain-of-custody?

-Karthik

Hi team / Ellen,

Thanks — I've put together a concise assurance playbook (summary below) and uploaded starter artifacts to a secure drive. The playbook will accompany the manifest and chain-of-custody template. High-level: 

- Scope: SOC 2 (CC1–CC8) mapped to customer-impacting surfaces; ISO 27001 reference controls included in the manifest. SIG responses will be provided as an annotated questionnaire (we'll flag N/A items).
- Provenance: each artifact will include: collector id, collector_host, collected_at_utc, file_hash (SHA256), and an assurance-signer (name/email). We'll provide a PDF "provenance statement" signed by our Assurance lead.
- Transfer: uploaded package available via short-lived Drive link (see related links) plus optional SFTP transfer. Drive link will be tenant-scoped and require MFA/ID check.
- Sampling: propose 7-day telemetry sample (UTC 2027-01-01 — 2027-01-07) for initial review; backup 90-day slice available on request.
- SLA: standard evidence turnaround is 72 hours; we can commit to 48 hours for this procurement through the close of deal (exceptions by mutual agreement).

I attached the chain_of_custody_template.docx; once you confirm transfer mode we'll populate the first two artifacts. Kimberly — please review the retention/escrow asks in RFP_addendum.pdf and advise if we should push back on 7-year retention.

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Assurance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
